title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not by Grothendieck. It is a typed English sheet, filed upside down in the box, numbered 'III.6' with a pencil '6' in the corner. It comes from someone else's typescript, probably a thesis or preprint of the mid-1960s, on sheaves of Azumaya ('central separable') algebras over a ringed space (X, O). It was presumably reused as scrap paper or filed among Grothendieck's motive notes. It is unrelated to the surrounding handwritten pages on effectivity structures, polarizations, I(G) → Eff(G) and motives.

The mathematics:
- Definition (implicit). An O-algebra L is 'locally separable' if:
  - L is locally of finite presentation as an O-module, and
  - each stalk L_x is a central separable O_x-algebra (an Azumaya algebra).
- Theorem III.6 (base change). If R is a commutative O-algebra, then L ⊗_O R is a locally separable R-algebra.
- Proof, step 1 (stalks). Stalks commute with tensor products. By Auslander–Goldman [4, Cor. 1.6], L_x ⊗_{O_x} R_x is central separable over R_x.
- Proof, step 2 (finite presentation). Locally there is 0 → P → O^n → L → 0 with P of finite type. Tensoring with R is right exact and gives P⊗R → R^n → L⊗R → 0. Since P⊗R is of finite type, L⊗R is finitely presented as an R-module.
- The text then recalls the commutant from [4]: for a ring Λ with centre A and a Λ-bimodule M, Hom_{Λ^e}(Λ, M) ≅ M^Λ = {m : xm = mx for all x ∈ Λ}. This prepares the commutant of a subalgebra Λ ⊂ Γ, to be sheafified in the next section.

This is the standard sheafification of Auslander–Goldman's theory, the setting of Brauer groups of ringed spaces and schemes (Grothendieck, 'Le groupe de Brauer I', 1966).
errors: 'a neighborhood U of X' should read 'of x' (typo in the original).
'has finite presentation as an R-algebra' should be 'as an R-module', which is what is actually proved and what the definition needs.

Minor gap: applying [4, Cor. 1.6] stalkwise requires the definition of 'locally separable' to include that each L_x is central separable over O_x. This is implicit and presumably given in the earlier pages of the typescript.

ideas.what: Base change of sheaves of Azumaya (locally separable) algebras along a commutative O-algebra R
ideas.modern_name: Stability of Azumaya algebras under base change
ideas.usually_credited_to: Auslander–Goldman (1960) for rings; Grothendieck (Le groupe de Brauer I, 1966) for schemes and ringed spaces

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of someone else's routine typescript on sheafified Auslander–Goldman theory, misfiled (upside down) among Grothendieck's notes on motives. It contains nothing new and nothing by Grothendieck himself.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down; the text is typed English, not Grothendieck's handwriting.
There is a handwritten '6' in the corner (sheet numbering), and there are faint pen marks near 'We know from [4' that are not text.
'neighborhood U of X' in the original should mathematically be 'of x'.
